citation: 8481.H. A. Berman and P. Taylor. 1978. FLUORESCENT PHOSPHONATE LABEL FOR SERINE HYDROLASES PYRENEBUTYL METHYL PHOSPHONO FLUORIDATE REACTION WITH ACETYL CHOLIN ESTERASE. Biochemistry 17(9): 1704-1713. BCI:BCI197866051619. Pyrenebutyl methylphosphonofluoridate reacts with [Torpedo californica] acetylcholineasterase to yield a conjugate with a stoichiometry of 1 fluorescent label/80,000 MW subunit. Kinetics of inactivation by the phosphonate and the subsequent reactivation behavior, as well as competition between the fluorescent compound and diisopropyl fluorophosphate, indicate that equivalent active site serines are involved in the labeling reaction. The long wavelength absorption band of the pyrene conjugate exhibits an 8-nm bathochromic shift, whereas its fluorescence emission spectrum shows little change. The shift correlates best with wavelength maximal observed for pyrenebutanol in solvents of high refractive index and is indicative of an association between the pyrene moiety and aromatic residues in the active center of the enzyme. Dynamic fluorescence quenching of the conjugated pyrene moiety by iodide, nitromethane and thallous ion is markedly reduced when compared with the corresponding quenching constants obtained for pyrenebutanol in solution. Quenching by thallous ion is most efficient and iodide is least efficient when quenching efficiencies for the conjugated fluorophore are considered relative to the free fluorophore. The absorption spectrum of the pyrene moiety overlaps with the emission specturm of the enzyme tryptophanyl residues and phosphonylation results in a quenching of the tryptophan fluorescence. Propidium, a peripheral site ligand, binds with equal affinity to the phosphonylated and native enzyme. Propidium binding results in 85-90% quenching of pyrene fluorescence. These findings show pyrenebutyl methylphosphonofluoridate to be a specific active site fluorescent label which can serve as a donor and acceptor of fluorescence energy. The conjugated pyrene appears to be buried in a region of high polarizability where it is restricted in contact with solvent and where the dominant electrostatic effect on pyrene would suggest an anionic subsite in the vicinity.

The capacity of certain unspecified fluorinated organic compounds (FC) to bind and release O2 and in CO2 in quantities greater than those present in the blood inspired was studied. Experiments were performed on anesthetized rabbits. The animal was tracheotomized and the trachea connected to a source of O2. During a period of stabilization, the vessels were incannulated to determine arterial and endotracheal pressure, pH, partial O2 (PO2) and CO2 pressure (PCO2). Succinylcholine was then administered to stop spontaneous respiration, after which ventilation was assured by rhythmic occlusion and opening of the O2 access tube. Pressure fluctuations were registered on an oscilloscope. After 30 min the lungs were flooded with a liquid fluorocarbonate compound (FC), through which O2 was caused to bubble. The FC was periodically returned from the lungs to the reservoir and reintroduced into the lungs. After 35 min a return to natural respiration was affected after aspiration of the fluorinated liquid from the lungs. During all these operations measurements of PO2, PCO2 and pH (arterial), arterial pressure, endotracheal pressure and an ECG were recorded.

Toxic effect of fluorides of alkaline earth metals on animals [rat, mouse, rabbit] consisted of impairment of the neuroendocrine system, mineral metabolism and functional state of the liver and kidneys. In intratracheal penetration of fluorides, slowly progressing toxico-chemical pneumosclerosis developed. BaF2 produced the most pronounced general toxic and fibrogenic effects. citation: 8528.J. C. Kouyoumdjian, M. F. Belin, J. Bardakdjian and P. Gonnard. 1976. ACTION OF SOME FLUORINATED AMPHETAMINE-LIKE COMPOUNDS ON THE SYNAPTOSOMAL UPTAKE OF NEURO TRANSMITTERS. Journal of Neurochemistry 27(3): 817-819. BCI:BCI197865072676. Two cyclic fluorinated compounds, fenfluramine (N-ethyl-.alpha.-methyl-P-trifluoromethyl phenylethylamine) and Lilly 110140 (P-trifluoromethylphenoxy-N-methyl-3-phenylpropylamine HCl), are specific inhibitors of the uptake of serotonin (5-HT) by synaptosomes. Amphetamine and some derivatives which are effective on the 5-HT system also affect catecholamine metabolism. The effects of different fluorinated derivatives were considered on the synaptosomal uptake of serotonin and dopamine (DA) and their precursors and GABA [.gamma.-amino-buryric acid] and its precursor, in order to determine the specificity of their action in this system. In vivo experiments, fenfluramine, 30 mg/kg, or Lilly 110/40, 10 mg/kg, was administered i.p. to a group of 8 rats. The effects of different compounds on the synaptosomal uptake in vitro, under the experimental conditions described, are summarized. Amphetamine strongly inhibited 5-HT uptake and slightly inhibited DA uptake. However the uptake of other substrates was not modified. The presence of the -CF3 function in the m-position provoked a marked inhibition of 5-HT uptake and a perceptible inhibition of DA and GABA uptake. The compound with a methyl group on the nitrogen (methylamphetamine) had the same effect as amphetamine. The presence of 1 methyl group on the nitrogen of 2 fluorinated compounds reduced both 5-HT and DA uptake. The presence of 1 ethyl group on the N of 3 fluorinated compounds provoked a strong inhibition of 5-HT and DA uptake. Fenfluramine acted on all the compounds studied. The fluorinated compounds in which the amine function was acetylated did not affect the uptake of the different substrates. Lilly 110/40 compound provoked a pronounced inhibition of the uptake of all the substrates. In vivo, 4 h after i.p. injection of fenfluramine, a marked inhibition of 5-HT and DA synaptosomal transport was observed, but no effect on the uptake of their precursors tryptophan or tyrosine occurred. The uptake of both GABA and glutamic acid (Glu) were reduced.

The ultrastructure of Purkinje cells was studied in rats that underwent protracted treatment with NaF (0.35 mg/kg body wt). citation: 8532.J. Brodeur, P. Paquin, L. Authier, D. Geadah, M. Yamauchi and M. G. Cote. 1976. INFLUENCE OF PHENO BARBITAL PRE TREATMENT ON METHOXYFLURANE AND SODIUM FLUORIDE NEPHROPATHY IN FISCHER 344 RATS. Toxicology and Applied Pharmacology 37(2): 349-361. BCI:BCI197662069937. Adult male Fischer 344 rats were used to investigate the effect of phenobarbital on methoxyflurane- and sodium fluoride-induced nephropathy. Pretreatment consisted of the i.p. administration of phenobarbital sodium at a dose of 50 mg/kg per day for 5 days; control animals were given saline. Pretreated animals were exposed to anesthetic concentrations of methoxyflurane during a period of 2 or 4 h, whereas other pretreated animals were exposed only to O2, the methoxyflurane carrier gas. For comparative purposes, other pretreated animals received NaFl in saline at doses of 0, 4.2 and 8.4 mg/300 mg. Phenobarbital pretreatment enhanced the nephrotoxicity of methoxyflurane as evidenced by a significant interaction between phenobarbital and methoxyflurane on plasma concentrations of Na and K, urinary volume, urinary excretion of urea and urinary concentration test. In contrast, the nephrotoxidity of sodium fluoride was not affected by phenobarbital. The urinary concentration test is a reliable monitor of the potentiating effect of phenobarbital on methoxyflurane nephrotoxicity.

citation: 8533.W. Meissner. 1976. THE EFFECT OF SELENIUM AND FLUORINE ON OSBORNE MENDEL RATS WITH RESPECT TO CARIES AND TOXICITY. Zentralblatt fuer Bakteriologie Parasitenkunde Infektionskrankheiten und Hygiene Erste Abteilung Originale Reihe B Hygiene Krankenhaushygiene Betriebshygiene Praeventive Medizin 162(3-4): 330-349. BCI:BCI197865024480. The influence of Se-containing drinking water on caries was studied using 100 Osborne-Mendel rats. The animals were divided into 5 experimental groups of 20 rats each. Se was tested in different doses as an addition to drinking-water as Na2SeO4 and in combination with a toothpaste containing NaF. Toxicity was determined by water consumption, mortality and body weight. In the 1st experiment 3 groups received Na2SeO4 in doses of 1, 5 and 10 ppm in the drinking water and the cariogenic diet Stephan 580. Two other groups served as controls, one receiving the cariogenic diet Stephan 580 and the other one getting the normal breeding diet. The analysis of variance carried out for the assessment of caries and the rest of Scheffe only show a different attack concerning those groups receiving the cariogenic diet and the control group fed with the breeding diet Altromin R. Nine of the 40 animals of the groups that had received the Se doses of 5 and 10 ppm did not survive the experiment. The average value of the water consumption and the body weight of the animals of the Se group was below the average of the remaining groups, which points out a strong toxicity of Na2SeO4. In regard to the water consumption, however, one cannot exactly define, whether it is an effect of the Se or of the cariogenic diet. All groups of the 2nd experiment received the cariogenic diet Stephan 580; 2 of them got Na2SeO4 in doses of 4 ppm in their drinking water. The molars of the lower jaws of one of these group were brushed with a tooth-paste containing NaF. The molars of the other group were treated with a paste, serving as a placebo. Two other groups were provided each with the paste containing F and the paste serving as a placebo, but without Se in their drinking water. Another 20 animals were used as a control group. The analysis of variance showed the widely known protective effect of the F by the statically significant different distribution of the caries. Comparing those 2 groups whose drinking water contained Na2SeO4 with the 2 other groups whose molars were treated with the paste containing F and the one serving as a placebo, respectively, it is concluded that Na2SeO4 has no influence on the protective effect of the F. A comparison of the group treated with the paste serving as a placebo with the control group showes that toothbrushing obviously has no great effect. With respect to the body weight at the end of the experiment one cannot demonstrate a clear effect using the linear contrast of Scheffe, and there also is no influence of Se on the total water consumption, which coincides with the results of the 1st experiment. The 2 experiments showed that Na2SeO4 is toxic in the doses applied. It has no influence on caries in Osborne-Mendel-rats and it does not harm the caries-restricting effect of F.

Arch Int Pharmacodyn Ther 171((1)): 240-242. BCI:BCI19684900084123. The mechanisms of fluorine metabolism are reviewed. The toxicity of 5-fluorotryptophane is linked to the formation of fluoro-acetate by enzymes participating in the normal catabolism of tryptophane. citation: 8672.R. F. Brewer, M. J. Garber, F. B. Guillemet and F. H. Sutherland. 1967. The effects of accumulated fluoride on yields and fruit quality of Washington navel oranges. Control trees were sprayed with .0025N NaCl to eliminate Na as a factor in the experiment. The LD50 of di-isopropyl phosphorofluoridate (DFP) for mice by the intraperitoneal route is 6.8 mg/kg while that by the subcutaneous or intravenous route is much lower (3.8 and 3.4 mg/kg respectively). When radioactive di-isopropyl phosphorofluoridate (DFP32) is injected to mice or rats by the intraperitoneal route there is a higher uptake of radioactivity in the liver with a corresponding reduced incorporation in other organs than when the administration is by the subcutaneous or the intravenous routes. citation: 8685.A. S. Lapik. 1965. Experimental study of the toxicity of certain fluorinated aromatic compounds. I. Acute toxicity of monofluoro-benzene. ortho-. meta. and paradefluorobenzene. hexafluorobenzene. pentafluoraniline. pentafluorophenol. Izv Sibirsk Otd Akad Nauk Sssr Ser Biol Med Nauk 3(#issue#): 91-94. BCI:BCI19684900062418. Results are given of an investigation of the acute toxicity of some fluorinated aromatic compounds: monofluorobenzene (C6H5F), ortho-, meta-, and para-difluorobenzene (C6H4F2), hexafluorobenzene (C6F6), pentafluoraniline (NH2C6F5), pentaf luorophenol (C6F5OH). The experiments with the fluorinated derivatives were carried out on mice of both sexes of the genetic line braun, 5-6 months old, weighing 18-20 g. The mice were exposed for 2 hr. to the vapors and observed for 48 hr. The experiments with pentafluoraniline and pentafluorophenol were performed on mice and rats, the former being administered as a 4% solution on mineral oil intraperitoneally and pentafluorophenol as a 2% aqueous solution subcutaneously in the region of the right thigh. Each dose of the compound was tested on 6 animals to determine acute toxicity. LD50 was calculated by the probit method. Monofluorobenzene, meta-and paradifluorobenzene did not differ from benzene with respect to the clinical picture of acute toxicosis. Unlike these compounds ortho-difluorobenzene in the same concentration (10-65 mg/liter) caused a more profound inhibition of the central nervous system. Hexafluorobenzene in a dose of 35-40 mg/liter caused in the mice sedation and sleep, and in a dose of 95-110 mg/l suppressed respiration and ultimately led to death from paralysis of the respiratory center. Pentafluoraniline in a dose of 100-150 mg/kg lowered the animals' body temperature by 1-1.5[degree], limited spontaneous respiratory activity, and partially suppressed the orienting reflexes. Larger doses, 300-450 mg/kg, led to more pronounced inhibition of the central nervous system and lowered body temperature by 6.7[degree]. citation: 8690.L. E. O. Spira. 1962. Bronchotetany presenting as bronchial asthma in a case of chronic fluorine poisoning. Ann Allergy 20((2)): 115-125. BCI:BCI19623900002376. Fluorine is a nerve poison whose long-continued action involves precipitating calcium salts in the body by way of the parathyroids, thus giving rise to latent tetany. When affecting the vegetative nerve supply to the muscles and mucous membranes of small bronchi and bronchioli, it causes bronchotetany as manifested by asthmatic attacks. A patient who had suffered for many years from chronic fluorine poisoning, resulting from protracted ingestion of fluorine contaminating practically every article of normal food and drink, became a victim of asthmatic attacks. Rigid treatment directed against fluorosis brought about a cessation of the attacks of bronchospasm and of certain other reversible signs and symptoms of latent tetany. Relaxation of the regime led to a recrudescence of the tetanic condition, with bronchitis and dyspnea as well as nocturnal cramps in the calves and paraesthesiae in the hands and fingers. Fluorides enter the body in variable quantities, being widely used in agriculture and in modern food industries as insecticides, sprays, preservatives, etc. It is, however, not the concentration of the noxa in any one article of food or drink, but the amount of fluorine ingested in the course of the day which is capable of causing illness. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: Author

citation: 8695.J. M. Neuhold and W. F. Sigler. 1960. The effects of sodium fluoride on carp and rainbow trout. Trans Amer Fish Soc 89((4)): 358-370. BCI:BCI19613600016316. The symptoms of acute fluoride intoxication in carp and trout include lethargy, violent and erratic movement, and death where there is partial or complete muscle contraction. Excessive mucus production associated with an increase in mucous cells in the epithelium of the head region and the gills also occurs. Changes in the electrophoretic pattern of the serum proteins in carp blood are evident. There is an increase in the fluoride concentration of the bones and a hypertrophy of the ultimobranchial gland. Rainbow trout embryos display initial symptoms similar to adult fish, including lethargy, violent movement, and tetany. Eupturing of the chorion by the embryo is attributed to violent movement during the onset of intoxication. Lethal doses and the sensitivities of fish to the toxin are dependent on several variables including size of fish, temperature of medium, and calcium and chloride concentration of the medium. It was demonstrated that there is an uptake of fluoride in muscle tissue, cancellous bone, and skeletal bone, and that uptake was increased when there was a rise in the fluoride concentration of the medium. The uptake of fluoride by the bone was via a second-order reaction and is assumed to be an enzymatic process. Proliferation of mucous cells in the epithelium of the gills and the head region is postulated to be instrumental in the excretion of fluoride from the body, and is considered an effective defense mechanism against fluoride intoxication. Hypertrophy of the ultimobranchial gland is thought to result from a deficiency in calcium induced by the effects of fluorides. The uptake of fluoride by the bone is a defense mechanism against fluoride intoxication and is postulated to occur with the elimination of fluoride from body circulation. This fluoride forms a stable mineral complex. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: Authors

Sciatic nerve of Rana nigromaculata with blood circulation was stimulated supramaximally at frequencies of 10, 20 and 50 cps, and the muscle action potential (M Wave) was recorded from surface electrodes on the gastrocnemius muscle. Stimulation for 3 min. before and after 3 min. rest was named "stimulation before rest" and "stimulation after rest" respectively. In studies on fatigue it was established that no difference of changes in action potential due to inequality of body weight occurred when the weight of frogs ranged from 20 to 50g. Influence of NaF on muscle fatigue: NaF was administered 0.15 mg, 0.10 mg and 0.05 mg per gram of body weight, (i) The initial action potential, caused by "stimulation before rest", of the NaF-administered leg was not significantly different from that of the control leg in which NaF was not administered, with the exception of the group which was given 0.15 mg/g of NaF and stimulated with 50 cps. (iii) The initial action potential caused by "stimulation after rest" in the NaF-groups showed higher values in the group receiving stimulation with 50 cps than in the groups stimulated with 10 and 20 cps. From these findings, muscle fatigue due to NaF administration is suggested to be contraction fatigue. (iv) At 15 min. after NaF was administered immediately after completion of one series of stimulation, another series of stimulation was given on the homolateral leg and on the contralateral leg respectively. In the former case the action potential was observed to drop more markedly than in the latter case. (v) At 36 min. after completion of the 2d series of stimulation (given on the homolateral leg to the 1st series), the 3d series of stimulation was given on the homo-lateral leg, and this caused still more drop of the action potential. The degree of counteraction was most marked with the lowest dose of NaF and was greater when MgSO4 was given before NaF than when it was given after the NaF effect had developed. The I method makes it possible to demonstrate min. changes of the cytoplasmatic ribonucleoproteins. It makes it possible to recognize pathological processes, if nuclear changes are used as criterion. 43 references. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: Courtesy Chem. Absts

citation: 8701.R. Sakuraba, T. Iwami and K. Ninomiya. 1958. Effect of sodium fluoride on the blood vessels. Hirosaki Med Jour 9((3)): 446-448. BCI:BCI19603500006846. Sodium fluoride, when given intravenously to cats, markedly reduced blood pressure by combining with serum Ca, but thereafter blood pressure rose comparatively rapidly to the normal level or more. NaF has been reported to produce gastrointestinal symptoms. Such a stimulating effect on the smooth muscle could readily be the cause of the rise in blood pressure. The vessel action of the drug was studied on vessel preparations cf frog and rabbit's ear. Neither 0.005%, nor 0.01% NaF solution caused contraction of the vessels, while both 0.02%, and 0.05% solutions produced noticeable vaso-constriction which tended to return to normal slowly. The vasoconstric-tion was not affected by imidalin nor acetylcholine. No interrelation between the vasoconstriction produced by NaF and the autonomic nerves was found. These results indicate that NaF produces vasoconstriction by stimulation of blood vessels in the stomach and intestine. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: Auth. summ

citation: 8702.D. K. Myers. 1956. Studies on cholinesterase. 10. Return of cholinesterase activity in the rat after inhibition by carbamoyl fluorides. Biochem Jour 62((4)): 556-563. BCI:BCI19573100016710. The initial inhib-itory reaction between the true cholinesterase of rat brain and NN-dimethyl- or NN-diethyl-carbamoyl fluoride is similar to that observed with the organophosphorus esterase inhibitors. Reaction with the dimethyl compound reaches an equilibrium quickly, whereas inhibition by the diethyl compound increases continuously for several hours. After injection of the carbamoyl fluorides into rats, the esterase activities recover completely; recovery follows the exponential curve of a first-order reaction. Rate of recovery is independent of the tissue in which the esterase is located, but differs from one esterase to another. All 4 esterases studied recovered more slowly after inhibition by diethyl compound. An attempt was made to analyze the reaction of the inhibitors with cholinesterase in terms of the rate constants involved in the Michaelis constant K1 = (k2 + KD)/k1 (cf. Briggs and Haldane, 1925). It is suggested that k2 may not have a large value. The mechanism by which the carbamoyl derivatives inhibit the esterases is similar to that proposed for the organophosphorus derivatives. Differences in the return of the cholinesterase activity after inhibition by the carbamoyl and by the organophosphorus derivatives are discussed in terms of the structure of the enzyme active center. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: Auth. summ

citation: 8705.A. H. Craige. 1952. Fractionation of the calcium in bovine blood by fluoride precipitation. Amer Jour Vet Res 13((46)): 31-37. BCI:BCI19522600017452. The precipitation of Ca from aqueous soln. by soluble fluoride is obstructed by the presence of certain anions (e.g. bicarbonate, citrate, borogluconate). This principle has been applied to the study of Ca in bovine blood, whereby results are expressed as a fluoride-precipitable or "free" Ca and a fluoride soluble or "bound" Ca fraction. Intraven. Na3 citrate in normal cows confirms the implication that this anion may account for variations in the "bound" Ca, and indirectly also in the "free" Ca fraction, although obviously it does not exclude the possibility of other "citrate-like" factors. Intraven. CaCl2 caused a much greater rise in "free" Ca in the blood of cows than did Ca borogluconate, which was anticipated and is in accord with the difference in the physical reaction to these salts. The "free" Ca, which in normal, stable-fed cattle ranged from 5.2 to 6.4 mg./100 ml., was reduced to less than 5 mg. in ketosis, and less than 4 mg. in milk fever. These levels reflect the degree of central depression, for cows with ketosis are sluggish and sleepy, whereas milk fever is characterized by coma and prostration. Luxuriant spring pasture is associated with a definite rise in "bound" Ca, and a tendency for the "free" fraction to be reduced. Limited observations of parturient cows indicate that both fractions tend to be reduced, contributing to the well-known fall in total Ca at parturition. Procedure: About 40 ml. of blood are collected in a tube containing heparin with a minimum of obstruction to flow in the vein. Then 7 ml. of blood are blown from a pipet into the bottom of duplicate centrifuge tubes containing 12 and 16 mg. carefully dried NaF. These are stoppered immediately and shaken vigorously a full minute, set aside 15 min., then again shaken, the stoppers removed, and centrifuged at high speed. The remainder of the untreated blood is also centrifuged. Specimens of 2 ml. each taken from all tubes are examined for Ca. The mean of the 4 tubes with NaF is taken as the "bound" Ca. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: A. H. Craige, Jr

citation: 8708.J. T. Irving. 1943. The action of sodium fluoride on the dentin and predentin of the incisor teeth of rats consuming diets containing calcium and phosphorus in various ratios. Jour Dental Res 22((6)): 447-456. BCI:BCI19441800013538. This paper records the studies of the early action of fluorine on the incisor teeth of rats consuming diets of normal, high and low Ca:P ratio (diets 1, 2 and 3 respectively). A hypercalcified line was first seen 18 hrs. after NaF inj. in ths distal predentin of the incisors of rats on diet 1. Measurements showed that the first part of this stripe was formed in predentin which was being laid down at the time of the inj. The stripe moved outwards with the incremental growth of the dentin and was preceded by a hypocalcified layer and the calciotraumatic line of Schour, Chandler and Tweedy. These latter 2 zones were formed in predentin laid down up to 16 hrs. before the NaF injection. In addition, a fine calcified line was found at and after 18 hrs. in the extreme proximal predentin; it was also formed at the time of the inj. The wide predentin of animals on diet 2 showed no calcification changes after NaF inj. The dentin had a hypercalcified stripe when the animals were allowed to live long enough for the matrix forming at the time of the inj. to become calcified. The proximal labial predentin of animals on diet 3 showed a fine calcified line 12 hrs. after the inj. of NaF. This moved outwards with the incremental growth of the predentin and later a similar line was seen in the proximal lingual predentin and finally in the intermediate predentin on both sides. Measurements showed this line to be present in predentin forming at the time of the inj. The animals on this diet were very liable to tetany after NaF inj. The above results are discussed with relation to the action of fluorine on the teeth and to some problems of dentin calcification. It is concluded that fluorine acts primarily by altering the composition of the blood and that the calcification changes produced thereby are variants of the normal process. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: Auth. summ

citation: 8709.J. Runnstrom, R. Gurney and E. Sperber. 1941. On protection against the inhibiting action of fluoride. Protection conferred by substrate in the respiration and fermentation of bakers' yeast. Enzymologia 10((1)): 1-39. BCI:BCI19451900016948. Respiration of yeast is reduced by addition of fluoride before glucose, but remains unchanged when the glucose is added before F. This inhibition is enhanced by increasing F concs. and time lapse between F and glucose additions. Under some conditions of low F concs. when F addition precedes glucose and where glucose precedes F, stimulation of fermentation occurs. At low glucose concs. the protection varies directly with the glucose conc. Low F concs. added before glucose cause recovery of respiration of "starved" yeast suspensions, but above 25 mMol./l. inhibition is complete. "Starved" yeast can be "restored" by standing in glucose or trehalose soln. Pyruvic acid, trehalose, rabbit serum and alcohol protect yeast against F; arabinose and galactose do not. Yeast pretreated with glucose had additional protection against F. Anaerobic yeast fermentation is more sensitive to F than aerobic and, while the glucose protection acts similarly, the difference in behavior between "starved" and normal yeast is abolished, and alcohol does not exert a protective action. Yeast extract and NH4CI cause a decreased protection where glucose is added before F, but an increased fermentation without F. Increased fermentation itself, as caused by cysteine, does not increase sensitivity to F. Thioglycollie acid decreases protection by increasing the respiration sensitivity to F. Two enzymes, a respiratory enzyme and an enolase, are considered to be concerned and to have different protective levels. Only substrates attacked by respiration or fermentation serve as protective compounds and the protected units depend upon respiration and fermentation for formation and maintenance. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: W. C. Shank

citation: 8711.J. A. Cameron. 1940. Effect of fluorine on hatching time and hatching stage in Rana pipiens. Ecology 21((2)): 288-292. BCI:BCI19401400009920. Tadpoles reared in well water containing 1 p.p.m. of F hatched precociously but at an earlier developmental stage than those reared in pond or distilled water. The pond-water tadpoles were the last to hatch; those in distilled water had reached the most advanced stage of development at the time of hatching. Histological examination showed that hatching was due in each case to the activity of the hatching glands. There was no evidence of any direct effect of the water on the egg envelopes. F probably retards development and also accelerates hatching. The differences observed between the behavior of the pond water and dist. water embryos may be due to the different kinds and amts. of dissolved material in each, particularly to variation in their Ca-Na ratios. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: J. A. Cameron

citation: 8712.P. H. Phillips, F. J. Stare and C. A. Elvehjem. 1934. A study of tissue respiration and certain reducing substances in chronic fluorosis and scurvy in the guinea pig. Jour Biol Chem 106((1)): 41-61. BCI:BCI19361000013611. A study was made of the physiological effects of fluorosis and of scurvy upon the distribution of reducing substances of the body and upon the tissue respiration of several tissues of the guinea pig. Titration with 2:6-dichlorophenolindolphenol showed that ascorbic acid was widely distributed throughout the body and was concentrated in the anterior lobe of the pituitary and in the suprarenal gland. The quantity of ascorbic acid present was directly proportional to that of the diet. It was further shown that: The rates of O uptake of liver tissue and the inhibiting effects of cyanide are not significantly different for liver tissue obtained from scorbutic, fluorine-poisoned, or normal guinea pigs. De-rolorization time of methylene blue by extracts prepared from liver tissue from scorbutic, fluorine-poisoned, or normal guinea pigs is not significantly different. The rate of O uptake, the inhibiting effect of cyanide, and the decolorization time of methylene blue are all dependent on the substrate in which they are measured. Succinate is most rapidly oxidized, lactate next, and formate and glucose differ little from plain buffer solution without added substrate. The indophenol oxidase content as qualitatively estimated by the coloration of the Nadi reagent is markedly diminished in the liver tissue of scorbutic and fluorine-fed guinea pigs as compared with normal controls, and the glutathione content increases, suggesting a compensating action on the part of glutathione. Cytochrome is present in the heart, kidney, and liver tissue from scorbutic, fluorine-poisoned, and normal guinea pigs. The rate of oxygen uptake of the suprarenal tissue from scorbutic and fluorine-poi-soned guinea pigs is about half that found in the tissue from normal control animals. In the case of two scorbutic animals (only two animals available) the oxygen uptake was increased to the normal value by the in vitro addition of ascorbic acid. The cyanide-inhibited fraction of the oxygen uptake of the suprarenal tissue is very low in scorbutic animals, high in fluorine-poisoned animals, and in general is proportional to the amount of vitamin C in the tissue. Ascorbic acid is definitely associated with a considerable portion of the cyanide-inhibited intracellular respiration of the suprarenal gland of the guinea pig. The similarity between scurvy and fluoro-sis is thus confirmed and extended by these researches. The evidence obtained indicates strongly that ascorbic acid deficiency and the deleterious effect of chronic fluorine toxicosis result primarily from disturbances in specific phases of cellular respiration. || ABSTRACT AUTHORS: P. H. Phillips

title: The distribution of a reducing substance (vitamin C) in the tissues of fluorine-fed cows
abstract: A reducing substance (vitamin C) was found widely distributed in the tissues, most in the suprarenal cortex and the anterior lobe of the hypophysis, very little in striated and heart muscle. Exposure of dogs, monkeys, and guinea pigs to dichlorodifluoromethane (A) and dichloro-tetrafluoroethane (B) showed both compounds to have a very low toxicity. "A" was the less toxic.
